column1: # Toy Story 3 Complete Edition on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Digital Eclipse's Octane engine on NVN, SDK 21.4.4, update v196608 (1.0.3); FMOD on its own AudioOut beside the SDK's audio renderer.
# 3,070 shaders, all in the .tfx effects of assets/effects/fx_new.zip (Octane zips, shader_split.py octane_shaders), all translate.
# Tested 2026-11-22 on a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra SM-S918B (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Adreno 740, Android 17) with the device's own driver:
# the publisher logos, the opening movie, the loading screens, the first level (the town, a mission done, Hamm and the aliens), the
# game's save across restarts and the pause menu, with the on-screen gamepad and with a controller. About 7 minutes of play in one run,
# no crash; [RED] lines left: one texture the deswizzle refuses (format 0x1, target 5; nothing seen missing) and the yield watchdog
# on the main thread, which waits for the game's render thread in Renderer::r_commitJobs (Sleep(0) polls, about 15% of a core in all).
# Without DM_VK_SCALED_FETCH=1 (below) every skinned character is invisible: their bone indices are R8G8B8A8_USCALED, which the
# Adreno 740 cannot fetch, so their pipelines were skipped (Woody and Bullseye missing, the game looked first-person).
# Frame rate: 30 fps as on the Switch; frame work p50 29 ms / p90 35 ms, 2.6% of frames dropped over 11,547 frames. The game's render
# thread takes a whole core (the X3, cpu7) and the S23 Ultra held it at 1.84 of 3.36 GHz at 69.5 °C, which is where the drops come from.
# --mt-replay is worse here (same device and level): 12.6% of frames dropped against 2.6% without it, frame work p90 42-48 ms. Keep it off.
